observations.iOSAccountControls: Passed on the base, client-only and composed trees. Real confirmation and TaskSync, held exchange and confirmation generations, identity/scope/bearer/expiry refusal, confirmation 401, lost reply re-entry, restore and sign-out, account isolation, draft, photo and outbox parity, and 1 KiB transport cap.
observations.sharedOwnerRecovery: Passed on the exact composed tree. The real Apple HTTP adapter used loopback against the exact backend. A private file emulated the credential store across owners. Secure-write refusal prevented exchange, then cold restore kept the recovery purpose. Dropping the committed exchange response led to a 401 for the identical retry and ordinary sign-in with the staged replacement. The old proof and TaskSync grant were refused. The restored owner returned the original account and scope and re-opened identical workspace, draft, outbox, photo and legacy bytes. Dropped confirmation responses kept the scope locked until the same-generation GET succeeded. The confirmed replacement survived a new owner and could be acknowledged without losing the session.
observations.backendReplay: Passed pinned ordinary and recovery service regression on isolated loopback. The shared-owner fixture also observed exact SQLite account and scope identifiers and task, entry and photo rows before and after recovery. The fixture closed its listener and rebound port 8765.
